observation.visible_scene: An inverted reflection in a blue swimming pool of a white multi-story building with dark-framed windows and railed balconies, flanked by two palm trunks (one left-of-center, one at the right edge) whose fringed crowns appear as dark green shapes at the bottom of the frame. The water surface is the mirror; the building occupies the upper portion and the palm fronds the lower portion throughout.
visible_changes: The reflected image continuously wobbles and deforms: the building's straight edges, window rectangles, and balcony lines bend, stretch, and shift position slightly from frame to frame as the water surface undulates.
The dark palm-frond shapes at the bottom change silhouette and spread frame to frame, rippling and re-forming rather than translating as solid objects.

The two palm trunks and the overall left-to-right layout stay essentially fixed in position, indicating the apparent motion is reflection distortion on the water, not movement of the building or palms themselves.
No clear camera pan or zoom is evident; framing of the building and trunks remains consistent across the excerpt.
The rippling is gentle and ongoing at both crop boundaries, with no single discrete event (splash, landing, or stop) visible inside the segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: What is disturbing the water surface (wind, a swimmer, an object entering) is not shown; the cause of the ripples is outside this excerpt.
The actual upright scene above the waterline (the real building and palms) is never directly visible, only its reflection.
Events before t=0 and after t=3.2s are unknown; the clip is a temporal slice of a longer continuous shot.
uncertain_details: Whether there is any slight camera drift versus purely reflection-driven motion is hard to separate, since the background evidence is limited to the reflection itself.
The propagation direction and origin of the surface ripples cannot be determined from these samples.
Small vertical shifts of the reflected building edges may be reflection warping rather than camera movement.
